newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria grounds airline after plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria grounds airline after plane crash.

text.p: Nigerian authorities on Wednesday grounded a local airline whose Boeing 727 plane crashed two weeks ago killing all 142 on board.

"The minister of aviation Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh has ordered the immediate grounding of all operations of the Aviation Development Company (ADC) airline," said a statement from the minister's office in the capital Abuja.
"This measure has become necessary in order to allow proper investigation into the crash, unhindered by continuous operations of the airline," it added.

The ADC plane, flying from the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt, crashed into a lagoon in a mangrove jungle 40 kms (25 miles) northeast of Lagos. The wreckage was not found until 24 hours later.

Among the casualties were Nigerian social science professor Claude Ake, a prominent Costa Rican lawyer Joacquin Tacsan and about 30 other foreigners including British, Indian, Italian, American, French and Israeli nationals.
The rescue team has yet to recover the bodies.
The statement said the minister regretted stopping the airline's operations but added that "this action is in line with international practice."
The crash is the worst in Nigeria since September 1992 when a C-130 transport plane went down in swamps near Lagos, killing 173 people, mainly senior military officers.

Several crashes have occurred since in the vast West African country where flying has become hazardous after an economic downturn undermined any spending to modernise infrastructure, including landing facilities.
